key_facts: **Atrophic acne scars** follow collagen loss after inflammatory acne: **ice-pick**, **boxcar** and **rolling**.
Separate true scars from **post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation or erythema** (flat colour change, which fades).
Prevention matters most: treat acne early; scarring is a referral trigger under NICE NG198.
Treatments (TCA CROSS, subcision, lasers, microneedling) are specialist or cosmetic; aim for improvement, not removal.

sections.title: Overview

blocks.title: Scope: counselling and recognition
blocks.text: For the pharmacist/IP, this page covers recognising scar types, setting expectations, safety and referral. It is **not** a procedure how-to.

blocks: Acne scarring is fibrous remodelling after inflammatory acne. **Atrophic** scars follow collagen destruction; raised scars are covered on [Keloids and hypertrophic scars](condition:keloids-hypertrophic-scars). Scars are usually permanent but may soften with time or combined treatment. The psychological impact is often high, even when scarring looks ‘mild’.

sub: Some scarring affects many people with moderate to severe acne; risk rises with delayed treatment and picking.

ul: Inflammatory nodules and cysts cause net **collagen destruction**, giving **atrophic** scars.
Risk rises with acne severity and duration, delay in treatment, picking (acne excoriée) and smoking.
**Post-inflammatory erythema and hyper- or hypopigmentation** are colour change, not true scarring, but patients often call both ‘scars’.
**"Scars will fade completely"**: atrophic scars are permanent; colour marks fade.

sections.title: Pathophysiology and pathology
blocks: Deep inflammation **destroys collagen** faster than it can be rebuilt.

mech.t: Ruptured follicles release contents into the dermis, causing intense inflammation.
Healing lays down too little collagen, leaving a depression.
mech.caption: Atrophic scar types: ice-pick, boxcar and rolling.

mech.t: Fibrous bands pull the surface down in rolling scars (released by subcision).

head: Type
Appearance
Typical sites
rows: Narrow, deep, V-shaped; deeper than wide (about 60–70% of atrophic scars)
Round or oval depressions with sharp vertical edges
Wider, sloping edges, tethered by dermal bands
Flat brown or red marks; no change in skin contour

sub: PIH is very common and often more distressing than scars; higher procedure risk.

sections.title: Diagnosis and investigations
blocks: Clinical: history of acne plus scar morphology. Document **Fitzpatrick skin type**, whether acne is still active, and the patient’s goals.

head: Look-alike
Distinguishing clues
rows: Flat colour change, with no depression

sections.title: Management
blocks: Treat active acne **early and adequately** (see [Acne vulgaris](condition:acne-vulgaris)). **Scarring is a referral trigger** under NICE NG198. Treat active acne first, before any scar procedures.

head: Scar type
Options (specialist or cosmetic)
rows: **TCA CROSS** (chemical reconstruction of skin scars), punch excision or grafting
Resurfacing (fractional lasers, peels), punch techniques, microneedling
**Subcision**, dermal fillers or fat, microneedling, fractional laser

blocks: Combined, multi-session approaches are usual. Refer to dermatology, plastic surgery or a reputable aesthetic clinic, and explain that the aim is **improvement, not removal**.

ladder.t: Treat active acne **early and adequately**; scarring = refer (NG198).
Ice-pick: TCA CROSS, punch excision / grafting. Boxcar: fractional laser, peels, punch, microneedling.

blocks.title: Prescribing limits and pitfalls
list: **Skin of colour**: Higher PIH risk: experienced operator only.

refer.t: Scarring or significant distress at any acne severity (NG198).
Low mood or body dysmorphic concerns: mental-health support.

sections.title: Red flags and when to refer

ul: Scarring or significant distress at any acne severity: refer (NG198).
Low mood, anxiety or body dysmorphic concerns: signpost or refer for mental health support.
Permanent but improvable with combined treatment.

pearls: **Separate scar from pigment.** The treatments are different.
Check isotretinoin status before procedures: see [Cosmetic procedures](condition:cosmetic-procedures).

quiz.q: Which atrophic scar type is commonest?
How do you tell PIH from a scar?
quiz.a: PIH is flat colour change with no contour change.

quiz.q: What does NICE say about scarring?
quiz.a: Scarring is a referral trigger at any acne severity.
